# Trigger results

Routing checks for the [trigger queries](./trigger-queries.md). Append new rounds; never delete earlier rows.

- Round 4 simulation (2026-11-09): agents saw only the skill names and descriptions, mixed with 8 unrelated skills, and answered which skills they would load. Queries 1 to 20 and 21 to 34, three runs each: no run loaded an unexpected skill.
- Round 6 simulation (2026-11-09): 16 skills in view (8 ours, 8 unrelated), queries 1 to 40, three runs: no unexpected skill loaded and no near-miss loaded one of ours. Query 36 loaded only `ui-interaction-design` in two runs (a pass under the any-listed rule). Runs 1 and 3 were identical, so fewer than three independent samples.
- Round 8: queries 41 to 43 were added after a dry run found no routing path for cell editing and row menus. Round 9 simulated them (below).
- Round 9 simulation (2026-11-09): 16 skills in view (8 ours, 8 unrelated), queries 41 to 51, three runs (run 2 took the queries in reverse order), same model family. Queries 41, 42, 43, 44, 46, 47 and 48 loaded `ui-interaction-design` in all three runs; 45 loaded `ui-visual-craft` in all three; the near-misses 49, 50 and 51 (`useMemo`, a flaky e2e test, unused CSS) loaded no skill of ours. `ui-design-workflow` was never loaded for a request that adds a control (41 to 44, 47): the entry for those is the pointer from `ui-interaction-design` to workflow step 0. Competing descriptions the runs named: workflow against interaction (43, 44, 47), workflow against visual-craft (45), and the `ui-simplify` keyword "정리" against no skill (51). Queries 1 to 40 were rerun in round 10 (below).
- Round 10 simulation (2026-11-10): 16 skills in view (8 ours, 8 unrelated), all 66 queries of sets 1 to 5, three runs (run 2 took them in reverse order, run 3 started at query 34), same model family, descriptions unchanged since round 8. Every should-trigger query (42) loaded at least one listed skill in every run, and none of the 24 near-miss, should-not and manual-only queries loaded a skill of ours; `ui-guideline-maintenance` never loaded. The strict rule (no skill of ours outside the expected list) passed 51, 61 and 64 of 66. All strict failures are extra loads on should-trigger queries: `ui-design-workflow` as entry point on 13, 3 and 1 queries (its description covers any request that changes a screen), `ui-visual-craft` on query 1 in all three runs (the request says the screen looks plain) and `ui-concept-design` on query 59 in two runs (a new screen). Among the held-out queries 52 to 66 the strict failures are 54, 57 and 62 (run 1, extra entry-point load) and 59 (runs 1 and 2, extra concept load). The expected lists were not changed after the runs.

- Round 10 re-run (2026-11-10), after the round-10 edits to the descriptions of `ui-design-workflow` (a phrase about one named screen removed), `ui-visual-craft` (a high-contrast keyword added) and `ui-interaction-design` (bulk-selection keywords added). Same 66 queries, 16 skills in view, three runs (forward, reverse, start at query 34), same model family. Every should-trigger query (42) loaded a listed skill in every run again, and `ui-guideline-maintenance` never loaded. Two of 72 near-miss and should-not runs loaded a skill of ours (query 22 loaded `ui-interaction-design` in run 3; query 26 loaded `ui-design-workflow` beside `dataviz-typography` in run 1); the earlier simulation had none, which is within run-to-run variation but worth watching. The strict rule passed 50, 64 and 62 of 66 (earlier 51, 61 and 64: the same mean, 58.7). Strict failures are extra loads: `ui-design-workflow` as entry point on 13, 1 and 1 queries, `ui-visual-craft` on query 1 in all runs, `ui-concept-design` on query 59 in two runs, and a new one, `ui-interaction-design` on query 1 in all runs, which the new bulk-selection keywords cause (the request asks for a bulk-approve button, so the load is defensible; the expected list was fixed earlier and was not changed). Held-out queries 52 to 66: strict failures on 54, 57 and 62 (run 1) and 59 (runs 1 and 3). The simulated descriptions did not get better or worse on average.

Caveats: simulated routing, not the Copilot runtime; queries written by the skill designer (only set 5, queries 52 to 66, is held-out: 52 to 56 come from an independent reviewer, 57 to 66 were written without the description keywords, and all expected lists were fixed before a run); set 3 avoids the keywords added after round 4. Rerun the whole set after any description change.
